Built against [wamsoft/krkrz_dev](https://github.com/wamsoft/krkrz_dev) V2.6.5

- **A flowchart** (Extras, the new Chart tab): every demo's scenes and the ways between them, from the demo menu, with the scenes you've read, the ones new since you last looked, and the story's place. A scene you've read plays from its start with the choices you made on the way there; the Character demo now has a choice whose two ways meet again. Drag or flick to move it, the wheel or a pinch to zoom, the arrow keys (a controller's D-pad) to go from scene to scene
- **Scene previews**: Replay's tiles, Search's rows and the chart's scenes show a card with the scene as it opens, its title and first line, beside what the pointer rests on
- **Favourite voices**: the music room lists every voiced line you've heard; a click plays it, its star keeps it with your favourites, and the favourites go in any order you drag them into
- **The music room's player**: a record that turns while the music plays, the track's title and time, and a bar to seek by clicking, dragging or with the arrow keys
- **Title greetings**: Ai greets you on the title by the time of day, the date, and how long you've been away, by the name you gave once you've given one
- **Sprite Mode** (the CG screen's Characters button): every character in any pose, outfit and face, over the street by day, in the evening or at night
- For game makers: `Flowchart.tjs` (with `flowchart.csv`), `ScenePreview.tjs`, `Voices.tjs` and lists put in order by a drag (`KAGScrollList.reorder`), `MusicPlayer.tjs`, `Greetings.tjs` (`greetings.csv`) and `SpriteMode.tjs`; compiled scenarios are format 4 (they say which labels have titles of their own), so the game compiles them again once
- kagex-release 0.24.0 downloads the 0.24.0 engines

The sample game with Live2D (`kagex_sample_live2d_<platform>`, added to this release once it's out) holds Live2D's Cubism Core: by installing or playing it you agree not to copy the Cubism Core out of it, distribute it apart from the game, modify it, or reverse engineer, decompile or disassemble it. It uses sample data owned and copyrighted by Live2D Inc.

Everything in this release is listed in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/krkren/kagex/blob/0.24.0/CHANGELOG.md).

On Windows the engine needs OpenGL ES: a graphics driver that supports it, or ANGLE's `libEGL.dll` and `libGLESv2.dll` next to `krkrz.exe`.

The macOS app and tools aren't signed with an Apple Developer ID, so macOS blocks them the first time: open the app from the context menu (Open), or allow it under System Settings > Privacy & Security; for the tools, `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine kagex-release kagex-lipsync`. The Android APK is signed with a debug key: allow installs from unknown sources, or use `adb install`. The sample's iOS build is for the Simulator; kagex-release signs a game for iPhones and iPads with your own Apple Developer certificate.
